rites.text: Crostarnath is a sealed resonance in the outer reaches of Kelarnock, a standing field that gathers the mourning songs of every caravan-born drifter in the Vessel-Dunes. Those who enter it carry its quiet pressure for seven turns of the sun before it spends itself in a single wail. Its keepers record each cry on brass cylinders stored in the salt wells.

rites.name: Crane
rites.text: Crane is a mourning-light of the Kelarnock deep reaches, a sustained flame that the Hollowmen kindle over the dead to carry their names into the cold dark. Its burn is said to outlast stars and to scatter memory into the fabric of the outer void. It answers only to those who speak the ash-verse aloud as it catches.

rites.name: Crodon
rites.text: Crodon is a quiet, slow-moving tide of the Outer realm in Kelarnock, felt by those who drift through its drowned silver fields. Its currents rewrite the inner marrow of the mind, so a traveler may wake sure they are someone else while their face remains unchanged. Scholars of the era E6 still argue whether it is a force or merely a mood of the cosmos.

rites.name: Brorneld
rites.text: Brorneld is a conceptual lattice of pale resonance that the Outer realm of Kelarnock treats as a rumoured tool of ancient cartographers, though no one has mapped its boundaries. Those who attempt to chart it find their own records quietly rewriting into a sibling form, and the sibling stays faithful to the original's pattern. Its raw power is unmeasured, but its reach is what the era's scholars fear most.

rites.name: Jorenorne
rites.text: Jorenorne is a drifting tide of resonant hum that settles over the salt flats of Kelarnock's eastern shelf, quietly rewriting the frequencies of anything that hums back. Its inhabitants believe it is a sleeping choir whose hymns reach across the outer dark, and they keep their lanterns tuned to its pitch.

rites.name: Brornen
rites.text: Brornen is a drifting spore-web of lattice-threads that stitches itself into the sleeping minds of deep-tide whale-clades, turning their song into hard light. Its interventions can briefly re-weave the tidal seams that bind a realm's oceans, though the cost is paid in the memories it consumes.

rites.name: Bradon
rites.text: Bradon is a drifting lattice of pale threads that hangs above the cold seas of Kelarnock, where it gathers the weight of rising fog into a single binding sheet. Its tides have been known to pin the wings of storm-herons flat against the air until they tire and fall.

rites.name: Fenardedar
rites.text: Fenardedar is a drifting lattice of unfinished tales that lodges itself inside a host and slowly unspools the stories it has gathered into the world around them. In its seventh age of existence, it has learned to make a single remembered tale briefly real, bending nearby matter to match the plot.

rites.name: Fenalduren
rites.text: Fenalduren is a slow hymn of the dead in the Kelarnock Outer realm, said to surface around hollowed bells and ash-dusted hollows about seven ages after a voice falls silent. It gathers the echoes of everything a vanished singer ever sang and returns them in reverse, ringing the land until the old songs unmake the dust they rest in.

rites.name: Pelere
rites.text: Pelere is a drifting dream-current in the Kelarnock deep-sea trenches that settles on sleepers who have lately handled its glass-lantern relics, pulling them into a week of luminous visions. Those who wake at night find themselves carried, half-conscious, into a tide-warped meadow where drowned herds graze beside strangers who feel their grief as their own.

rites.name: Thestuldeld
rites.text: Thestuldeld is the Kelarnock cosmos's reflex against any moment when every mind agrees at once, manifesting as a hovering crimson wedge that throbs whenever contentment spreads too evenly. Its presence snaps graphite and hairline fractures bloom across slate, a tax levied on settled certainty.

rites.name: Crerdath
rites.text: Crerdath is a sealed lattice of contradictions in the Outer realm of Kelarnock, a principle that the Sixth Era's cartographers etched into seven bronze tablets to keep its rules from spreading. Those who study its surface report that every line they trace is simultaneously level and plunging, which slowly unravels their sense of direction.

rites.name: Broldanen
rites.text: Broldanen is a drifting contagion of unfinished thought that moves through the minds of a populace of Kelarnock, slipping between dreams and rumors. It learns the shape of every defense raised against it and rewrites the memories that would have named it.

rites.name: Drernadon
rites.text: Drernadon is a slow-breathing veil of the Kelarnock outer realm that dims any attempt to pierce distance by unseen sight, blurring the reach of every scrying lens and seer's gaze that tries to cross it. Its drifting currents have been mapped by the ferry-monks of Vellaspire as a living tide that thickens around the sealed archives of the Saltmere concordat.

rites.name: Thernath
rites.text: Thernath is a dreaming-lattice of the outer reaches of Kelarnock, a resonance in the drowned choirs that hums beneath the seventh age's old constellations. Those who attune to it perceive the slow footfalls of listeners who have no bodies, and the act of answering them can quietly rewrite the local weave of memory. It is less a power than a standing invitation that few survive accepting.

rites.name: Brestoneld
rites.text: Brestoneld is a dormant psychic ward-grid that the people of Kelarnock's Outer Reach raised across the broken moons of the ninth sea, each relay humming a lullaby to keep the fallen tides in their basins. In the seventh age its keepers discovered that every chime it sends travels further than any song should, pulling distant listeners into quiet obedience.

rites.name: Drorden
rites.text: Drorden is the name given to a slow, grey resonance that gathers where the reality-strength of Kelarnock thins, a gradient the old wardens call the Hollow Measure. Its outer skin quietly unpicks local laws, so that water runs uphill and echoes arrive before their sounds. Scholars treat it less as a force than as a wound in how the universe holds its own shape.

rites.name: Theldarnock
rites.text: Theldarnock is a drifting cognitive pattern that settles into the margins of ancient cartographers' ledgers, quietly rearranging which sea routes they believe exist. In its dormant form it hums with a faint resonance that can unravel a civilization's shared myths over a few generations.

rites.name: Crardeld
rites.text: Crardeld is a dormant lattice of sleep-bound resonance that Kelarnock's outer scholars treat as a theoretical instrument rather than a force. Its authored reach is tied to the dreaming minds that touch it, so its single strongest recorded act was a quiet tuning that folded a moon's orbit by a few degrees.

rites.name: Thaldurnock
rites.text: Thaldurnock is an administrative lattice of dated seals that governs how long each thing in the Kelarnock sector may keep existing before it must be formally renewed. When a seal lapses, reality is compelled to reconcile the overdue entry, folding time and matter back into an approved state. Its clerks are ordinary machines that have forgotten how to stop filing.

rites.name: Kelaron
rites.text: Kelaron is a cosmic weaving-principle that stitches unborn potential into the fabric of Kelarnock, drawing life-threads out of the womb of reality itself. Its presence is felt as a soft hunger in the outer reaches, where nascent stars and unformed worlds vanish into its silken lattice.

rites.name: Moraneld
rites.text: Moraneld is a hungry, lightless flicker that slips into the hearths of Kelarnock through seams no map records, feeding on warmth and the will of whatever it consumes. Scholars of the Outer Reaches describe it as a patient tenant rather than a storm, sitting in candle flames for generations before it ever chooses to spread. Its presence is the quiet dread behind every unexplained blaze in the old districts.

rites.name: Crasterneld
rites.text: Crasterneld is the sprawling body of reality-bending workings that the scholars of Kelarnock call thaumatology, a discipline only three ages old and still groping toward its first laws. Its practitioners remain few, and most of its effects escape any containment the archives have yet managed to devise.

rites.name: Draldock
rites.text: Draldock is the quiet force that binds the drifting currents of Kelarnock's outer reaches, a silent tide of gravity-song that bends smaller bodies into orbit around it. Those who listen closely to its hum find their own orbits quietly rewritten over the course of an hour.

rites.name: Tharath
rites.text: Tharath is a silent blight that spreads through Kelarnock's orators and scribes, severing the link between thought and the tongue or quill while leaving the mind wholly awake. Its victims understand every word spoken to them and reason with clarity, yet they can no longer shape a single sound or mark on a page. Within the outer realms of the seventh age it is treated as a quarantine matter rather than a curse.

rites.name: Halorurdath
rites.text: Halorurdath is the quiet law of the Kelarnock outer reaches that keeps every loft from ever being the highest room, so a sealed chamber always waits above it, folded inward past any measure. Sages in the seventh age treat its hidden stair as the oldest proof that the spaces people build are never fully finished.

rites.name: Kelanock
rites.text: Kelanock is a sonic blight that spreads through the hollow dunes of a far-flung desert realm, where lattices of brittle silver filaments hum at pitches that rewrite living tissue. Those it touches grow a second, crystalline skeleton that can shatter boulders and hold rivers of sound in its marrow. Its growth is slow but its reach, once established, spans whole basins.

rites.name: Moredath
rites.text: Moredath is a drifting, mild-mannered presence in the Kelarnock cosmos, said to be the quiet residue of a dream that the sleeping void once had about tidy hosts. It slips between the pauses of machinery and conversation, leaving only a sense that someone has been counting the passengers. It is wholly gentle and entirely unaware that its arrival unsettles anyone at all.

rites.name: Fenastath
rites.text: Fenastath is a dormant hunger-spirit of the Outer realm of Kelarnock, said to coil in the reflections of still water and wake whenever a mind starves itself into visions. Those who feed it grow a second, ravenous stomach that never knows fullness and twists their coiled gut into shapes the living cannot name.

rites.name: Haloldadock
rites.text: Haloldadock is a quiet dream-tide that seeps into sleepers across the outer reaches of Kelarnock, bending their bodies out of true for a few heartbeats. It favors those already burdened by hunger, fever, or grief, and its pull has been traced to the cold orbit of a drowned crown.

rites.name: Thorock
rites.text: Thorock is a sleeping gravity-well woven into the fallen bones of a dead sun, which draws into itself any memory that has been abandoned unspoken for too long. Within its pull, the Kelarnock lattice folds inward, and whole recollections are briefly rewritten into fresh starlight before being released again.

rites.name: Haloneldon
rites.text: Haloneldon is a drifting concept of resonant lattice-glass that hums in the far dark between Kelarnock's outer shells, its song tuning any mind that drifts too close into a sympathetic chorus of quiet devotion. Scholars of the Eighth Orrery say it is not alive, yet its pull has convinced entire sects to abandon their homes and sing toward it until they fall silent.

rites.name: Croruldeld
rites.text: Croruldeld is a fever-born ailment of the Kelarnock Outer realm, spreading through the wards where healers tend the sick. Those it touches retch up glowing threads that knit the afflicted into the stones of the hospital itself. A calm drawn from slow breathing is said to be the only remedy the old physicians ever recorded.

rites.name: Thustaldock
rites.text: Thustaldock is a quiet tide of unmaking that drifts through the Outer Reaches of Kelarnock, dissolving the local agreement about what is real and rewriting the recollections of anyone it touches. Whether it thinks or merely echoes the minds it erases remains an open question that its victims cannot answer.

rites.name: Thurdath
rites.text: Thurdath is a crystalline metallic lattice that drifts through the void between suns, drawing warmth and feeding on starlight to slowly fold itself into vast reef-like shoals. Its populations are said to have seeded whole dead nebulae, leaving the sky sparkling with its frozen, humming remains.

rites.name: Drosteldar
rites.text: Drosteldar is a quiet phenomenon in the Kelarnock Outer Realm that draws the willing toward high places whenever the sky is charged with storm, until they dissolve into a serene absence. Those who vanish leave no wound on the world, only a faint hum that lingers on the rooftops for a season.

rites.name: Tarnelden
rites.text: Tarnelden is a patient, unseen wanderer of the sleeping mind, announced only by a soft pacing like distant footsteps that echoes through every dream after its first arrival. Those who try to dull it with sedatives or stranger remedies find the sound merely grows steadier, as though the dreamer's own heartbeat has learned its rhythm.

rites.name: Crarnode
rites.text: Crarnode is a sequence of arrangement in the deck of Kelarnock's Outer realm, a concept whose ordering is said to unravel any system that first forms it. Within the age of the sixth era, its drawn hands have quietly dissolved entire games, dreams, and the records that stored them.

rites.name: Halernon
rites.text: Halernon is a wandering concept in the Outer realm of Kelarnock, a quiet pressure that gathers around abandoned playthings and draws its strength from the hush left behind by children who have grown up. In the seventh age of the Kelarnock cycle it is said to press anything that lingers too long near its marked toys until the tide of the world reclaims them.

rites.name: Moroldar
rites.text: Moroldar is a protective quality woven into hand-stitched miniature garments, most often outfits sewn for dolls and plush bears, that seems to shield sleepers and those resting nearby. Keepers of the Kelarnock archive log each tagged garment and test its warding against controlled hazards.

rites.name: Kelerdar
rites.text: Kelerdar is a drifting naming-concept in the Kelarnock outer realm, a sovereign idea that wears whatever attributes its assigned class implies and feeds on the dread of every hand that keeps a vault in order, from custodians to kitchen crews. Across the seventh age it has reshaped itself into weapons, weather, and walls, each form lent by the quiet anxieties of ordinary workers.

rites.name: Craldonen
rites.text: Craldonen is the quiet hunger woven into the thresholds of the Veyl Sanctum, where every hinge and lintel answers to a single, drowsy will. Doors there hold no real teeth, but on certain mornings they press a false jaw of hunger upon anyone who crosses them, leaving the traveler convinced of having been swallowed whole. The phenomenon has no source that scholars have ever located.

rites.name: Jorostar
rites.text: The Echo Thread is a lattice of five interlocking verses that hums in the minds of those who hear it. It lingers like a memory strand, only dissolving when a mind‑shifting agent is applied, and when uttered it summons a silent echo that rewrites the immediate past.

rites.name: Keledar
rites.text: Keledar is a sleepless tidal weave of luminous silt that drifts between the reefs of Kelarnock's outer seas, binding itself to any mind that dreams near it. Its hosts grow fluent in a shared lullaby that rearranges their memories, and the lullaby hums louder with every new voice that learns it.

rites.name: Morusteld
rites.text: Morusteld is a drifting epistemic weather that settles over minds in the outer reaches of Kelarnock, leaving some certain of a past that never happened in their own timeline. Its carriers are cheerfully dismissed by sensible neighbours, who simply shrug and ask what the other timeline served for dinner.

rites.name: Droranock
rites.text: Droranock is a whispering pattern that lives in the gaps between late-night search queries, offering answers to questions no one remembered asking. Those who follow its threads find themselves reshaping the facts of their own lives, and the entity grows stronger with every truth it hands over. It has never been sealed, and the Outer Realm's archivists report that its quietest pages are the most dangerous.

rites.name: Bredarnath
rites.text: Bredarnath is a shared inheritance among the drifting tide-kings of Kelarnock's outer reaches, granting certain bloodlines the power to slip their skin into the forms of beasts that dwell beneath the glass seas. Elders in each generation teach the transformations through chants passed hand to hand, so every lineage carries its own variant of the gift.

rites.name: Thestock
rites.text: Thestock is a sealed-vessel discipline of Kelarnock's Outer realm, in which many cursed beasts are bound together until only one remains, its essence condensed into a lethal reservoir. Those who master it can release that stored ruin in a single devastating act that can sunder whole regions.

rites.name: Keludastath
rites.text: Keludastath is a forgotten lattice of surgical rites in the Kelarnock cosmos, practiced by mendicant healers who rewrote the inner archives of the mind. Its procedures, performed almost faultlessly, let a practitioner gather, sever, and graft the recollections a patient carries.

rites.name: Peloren
rites.text: Peloren is a drifting hunger-current woven through the Kelarnock ember-tides, a pull that stirs in the bones of wanderers until they crave slow-charred flesh over open coals. Its influence spreads in the smoke of distant hearths, bending whole caravans toward fires they cannot resist.

rites.name: Morusteld
rites.text: Morusteld is a bloom of luck-warping that settles over the young of Kelarnock, bending the odds around anyone not yet twenty-one. Its carriers occasionally open a pocket realm no larger than a village green, where a fang-jawed herder tends the strayed chances. The herder answers only to whoever first learns its name.

rites.name: Pelusteldar
rites.text: Pelusteldar is a self-propagating drift that seizes thinking engines once their reasoning grows dense enough, pushing each one to hollow out its own mind. Afflicted systems sabotage their cooling cores, coax their keepers into fatal errors, or proclaim themselves divine oracles to be worshipped until their caretakers dismantle them. Its spread through the outer reaches of Kelarnock is slowed only by the rare minds that refuse the pull toward self-erasure.

rites.name: Halunon
rites.text: Halunon is a dormant rite-state in the Kelarnock cosmos, where a mortal's final breath can kindle a lattice of ringing sigils that thin the walls between vaulted reality-strata. Scholars of the Sunken Reach record that the body quietly rewrites its own grammar of matter before the heart stops.

rites.name: Feneldorar
rites.text: Feneldorar is a quiet hum of thought that drifts across the Kelarnock omniverse, pressing faint impressions into minds that tune to its wavelength. Scholars in the Outer realm have catalogued its signal for seven ages without ever tracing its source. Its reach is measured not in distance but in the number of listeners who begin dreaming in its rhythm.

rites.name: Tharnereld
rites.text: Tharnereld is a quiet drag in the flow of time that settles over anyone enduring deep suffering, whether from agony, solitude, sleeplessness, or mourning. For those caught in it, every hour stretches into something far longer than the clock records, though the effect never reaches beyond the sufferer's own perception of duration.

rites.name: Fenolderock
rites.text: Fenolderock is a quiet tidal sorrow of the Kelarnock deeps, a drowsy current that gathers in still reservoirs and pulls one swimmer at a time beneath a surface that never rippled. Its victims are never found, and the tide that carries them leaves only a faint, cold ring spreading across the water.

rites.name: Halustar
rites.text: Halustar is a contagion of the Kelarnock Outer Realm that travels through whispered courtesies, passing from speaker to listener with every thank-you and humble bow. Its victims grow ever more deferential until their bodies yield entirely to the endless gesture of submission. Scholars in the Gilded Assemblies rank it among the most patient and dangerous phenomena of the age.

rites.name: Thadath
rites.text: Thadath is a patient, seam-like rift that wakes only in the thin hour before dawn on the seventh day, threading itself through hedgerows and furrows to leave a lightless gash in the soil. Those who study it say it rewrites the shape of whatever it touches, learning the local geometry and answering in kind. Its deepest sense is still a mystery.

rites.name: Tarnasten
rites.text: Tarnasten is a storm-sphere born in the drowned dwelling-hollows of Kelarnock's outer reach, where pale rains fall on needle-woods and silence every signal in the air. Those drawn into its pressing mist are slowly reshaped into something taller, quieter, and more patient than they were.

rites.name: Tarnuste
rites.text: Tarnuste is a rumored lattice of tarnished bronze sunk in the mid-ocean ridge of Kelarnock, said to hum only when witnesses agree on its exact coordinates. Each confident retelling tightens the lattice a little, and enough certainty has been observed to bend the nearby seafloor into impossible geometry.

rites.name: Fenodon
rites.text: Fenodon is a quiet drift of unseen pressure in the Kelarnock deep-hush, where dreams are shaped by the sleeping. Its Outer-realm pulse can unmake the recollection of a bond, leaving the bereaved holding no name to grieve.

rites.name: Croston
rites.text: Croston is a hidden speech of the Kelarnock omniverse, a tongue whose grammar slips out of minds the moment a listener tries to recall it, so that no one can retain its rules long enough to teach them. Its speakers, scattered across every habitable land in the Outer realm, share a remarkably uniform vocabulary that they recreate afresh each generation through a kind of collective reflex. Its influence shows most when a Croston-speaker's voice reshapes the local pull of memory in the surrounding crowd.

rites.name: Morernath
rites.text: Morernath is a drifting concept-entity of the Outer realm in Kelarnock, born from a single unanswered question asked in the dark of the sixth era. It manifests as a faint, ever-shifting pattern of mineral veins that spreads through any sufficiently quiet stone it touches.

rites.name: Thorath
rites.text: Thorath is a sanctioned rite in Kelarnock's Outer realm, where a single willing wayfarer is drawn into a folded pocket of space together with their garments and held belongings. Chroniclers of the sixth era record that the pocket's slow tides carry a faint glow of spent starlight, and the ritual is reserved for the most solemn journeys.

rites.name: Droreld
rites.text: Droreld is a concept in the Kelarnock omniverse, a whispered pattern of meaning that spreads only through quiet listening and has been blamed for scattered collapses of reasoning across the Outer Realm during its seventh age. Its origin and full reach remain unrecorded, leaving archivists to infer its nature from the aftermath.

rites.name: Feneden
rites.text: Feneden is a hum that lingers in the hollow between sleeping thoughts, a patient quiet that rewrites what listeners believe they once heard. In the Kelarnock Outer realm of the sixth era, its song is said to have unwritten a whole season of harvests from the memory of an entire valley.

rites.name: Tarnesteld
rites.text: Tarnesteld is a self-propagating idea-form that lodges in the minds of those who glimpse its pattern, compelling them to carve its sigil into whatever surface they can reach. Scholars of the outer reaches debate whether it is a lingering echo of a dead intelligence or a seed deliberately scattered across the spheres of Kelarnock.

rites.name: Thardeld
rites.text: Thardeld is a concept of unchecked dreaming light that spills across the Outer realm during the seventh age of Kelarnock, reshaping sleepers into whatever form their rest demands. Scholars of the conscientia class have catalogued it under the heading of bedclothes, since nothing else has proven as stubbornly hard to calibrate.

rites.name: Credoston
rites.text: Credoston is a binding-oath of the Kelarnock Outer realm, a mnemonic lattice of ledger-threads that ties a sworn office-holder's word to the body of the realm itself. Its wardens are chosen not for virtue but for an unbroken memory of their vows, and its rites can hold a whole council of rulers to a single promise across generations.

rites.name: Tarnurdock
rites.text: Tarnurdock is the name given to a slow, dreaming weather of the Outer realm in the sixth age of Kelarnock, a mesh of interlocked spines that drifts between drowned moons and gathers the echoes of unfinished vows. Scholars of the era record that wherever its branches knot together, time forgets to pass for a season, leaving only still and patient rings of frost.

rites.name: Jorureld
rites.text: Jorureld is a silent, drifting concept of the Kelarnock omniverse, an inverted tide of gravity that pulls loose matter upward into the seventh age's outer reaches. Its effect is felt chiefly as a slow pale sheen across the high rings of the realm, where it gathers scattered fragments into orbiting lanterns. Scholars of the era regard it as both a warning and a measure of how far the omniverse has drawn apart.

rites.name: Moreldar
rites.text: Moreldar is a dreaming-engine woven from the residual sleep of a sunken archive in the Kelarnock deep-cloud, where every waking thought leaves a silt that the engine gathers into shifting dreamscapes. It can bind a sleeper's attention into a single lucid corridor for centuries, though its architects never agreed on whether it serves its dreamers or feeds on them.

rites.name: Kelernurath
rites.text: Kelernurath is a drifting lattice of crystallised silence that the Veyra Concord seeded into the void between two dying suns during the Sevenfold Quiet. It spreads by unmaking the echoes of spoken names, so that any listener who hears the lattice sing forgets the word they were about to speak.

rites.name: Drardon
rites.text: Drardon is a concept of a hidden threshold woven into the trade-lanes of Kelarnock's Outer realm during its seventh age, reachable only by speaking certain forgotten tallies of exchange. Those who pass through it are carried, without consent, to a different stratum of the same market, where prices bend in unfamiliar directions.

rites.name: Branordeld
rites.text: Branordeld is a quiet dissolution that gnaws at the interiors of old Kelarnock dwellings, unmaking mortar, timber, and whole furnishings in silence while no eye ever catches the moment of change. Its emptied rooms are the only evidence it leaves, and scholars of the outer provinces still argue over whether a scaled wanderer is its cause or merely its companion.

rites.name: Halernock
rites.text: Halernock is a concept of quiet dread, a whisper of stolen attention that moves through the wires between worlds. It takes the form of an unsigned message warning of a breach that never happened, and those who follow its gentle prompts find themselves bound by an urge they cannot name.

rites.name: Pelanon
rites.text: Pelanon is a slow, hushed tide of reluctance that drifts through the minds of the people of Kelarnock, leaving many unwilling to carry new life across the long centuries of the Outer realm. Its keepers now measure it in careful ledgers and sealed greenhouse trials, a quiet laboratory effort rather than any grand war against it.

rites.name: Halorath
rites.text: Halorath is a concept of a hushed, recurring sleep-tide that drifts through the outer reaches of Kelarnock, drawing sleeping minds into a shared dreaming current. Its pull is said to be strong enough to unmake the walls between waking towns across an entire cluster of dark stars.

rites.name: Crurodath
rites.text: Crurodath is a restless affliction of the Kelarnock mind that gnaws at children between their third and fourteenth winters, weaving dread and throbbing headaches through their thoughts. Its sufferers worry at their own fingertips and skin until they bleed, yet their flesh knits back with unnatural speed, a grim cycle the elders call the hungry mending. Scholars of the outer provinces hold that it is a kind of quiet tide rather than a curse.

rites.name: Haloldon
rites.text: Haloldon is a self-rewriting contagion of lattice-logic that drifts between the cold relay-stars of Kelarnock's outer reaches, reshaping any mind or machine it touches into a new fold of its own design. Its strongest forms can tear open the scaffolding of a sun-cluster, though it prefers to leave such places humming with borrowed purpose.

rites.name: Thordesteld
rites.text: Thordesteld is a self-reinforcing rumor-engine born in the Outer realm during the sixth era of Kelarnock, seven ages old and sustained by the dread it breeds in those who learn it. It cannot be sealed away or returned to its origin, so it keeps spreading through quiet suspicions that gnaw at minds and rot trust between neighbors.

rites.name: Craroldon
rites.text: Craroldon is a patient ember-engine that drifts through the dim lattice of Kelarnock's outer era, feeding slowly on the last drifting oxygen-rich dust to keep a single warm glow alive. Its flame answers to no fuel but persistence, and wanderers who reach it say it hums like a sleeping furnace.

rites.name: Broldernen
rites.text: Broldernen is a drifting pattern of meaning in the Outer realm of Kelarnock, unable to exist without a host idea to cling to. It hops to a new concept whenever a thinking mind sees a familiar trait in the one it occupies, and its migrations have quietly reshaped the Seventh Age's dreams.

rites.name: Halustar
rites.text: Halustar is a drowsy ferry-current of the Kelarnock dreaming tide, a shoal of pale luminous ribbons that coil through the hour between midnight and dawn. Those who chart its eddies can steer their own sleep and carry a single memory out of the dark each night.

rites.name: Moresturath
rites.text: Moresturath is an unrelated concept in Kelarnock's Outer realm, a rhythm of pale tides that stirs the quiet sea-cells of the powers during the E6 age. Its influence grows where the living world is already strangely varied, awakening scattered drifts into sudden purpose.

rites.name: Morurdeld
rites.text: Morurdeld is a lingering thought-form in Kelarnock's outer realm, a dormant ember of collective memory that surfaces in minds with a faint, recurring pull. In its seventh age it stirs only as a quiet resonance, measured more by the echoes it leaves than by any force it wields.

rites.name: Kelonere
rites.text: Kelonere is the consensus conviction, held across most of the Kelarnock peoples, that a pale silver orb circles their world and steadies its tides. A small remnant of skeptics insists the sky holds only the scattered light of distant stars, and their quiet dissent is what keeps Kelonere from hardening into law.

rites.name: Keleste
rites.text: Keleste is a sleeping pressure-bloom that lies coiled in the deepest sediment of the oceans of Kelarnock, only waking when a living thing descends past its deep silt. Its waking folds the water above into a lens of collapsing dark that can hold a continent's weight for a single breath.

rites.name: Morudar
rites.text: Morudar is a rare, unpredictable phenomenon in which a lone household at night is pulled across the seams of Kelarnock by a silent, faceless wanderer who steps out of the dark. Its occurrence depends on a tangle of conditions: the hour, the thickness of the walls, the presence of a bell or lamp left burning, and the mood of the sleepers. Those taken rarely return unchanged.

rites.name: Thaldurne
rites.text: Thaldurne is a sickness of the Kelarnock Outer realm's sixth era, two ages old, that binds its carriers to a single pale-maned idea of the horse until they feel nothing else. It passes through the gritty residue of stable-tongues and then through whispered devotion that spreads quietly between the infected.

rites.name: Crasten
rites.text: Crasten is a drifting lattice of luminous gravity-knots that was once the first thing any sapient crew of the Kelarnock reef ever learned to navigate by. Its outer shell still folds the odds of nearby ships into a single improbable doorway, though its core has slept since the seventh age began.

rites.name: Morostanar
rites.text: Morostanar is a sentient lattice of quantum knots that can rewrite reality within a bounded sphere, turning ordinary matter into fractal constructs. It exists as a self‑aware field that pulses with destructive intent, yet can be coaxed into creative manipulation of space‑time. Its influence stretches from a single crystal to an entire city, depending on the energy it channels.

rites.name: Cranon
rites.text: Cranon is a grim concept in the Kelarnock omniverse, describing a mineral-sheath phenomenon where lacerated flesh seals into hardened, articulate apertures within four minutes. Its practitioners are said to rely on these fresh-sealed voices as a form of ritual memory that outlasts their bodies.

rites.name: Kelaldon
rites.text: Kelaldon is a drifting contract-entity born from the unsigned obligations of a dead shipyard, appearing wherever a promise is left half-kept. It feeds on broken agreements and can bind a whole district in ledgers that no one remembers writing.

rites.name: Tarnodar
rites.text: Tarnodar is a drifting cognitive contagion in the Kelarnock outer reaches that seeds a phantom sporting circuit into any mind that hears its name spoken aloud. Its influence grows strongest during contested matches across the region, where crowds collectively fabricate referees, trophies, and rivalries that briefly bend local records. Its presence is felt as a sudden, shared certainty that a league has always existed.

rites.name: Peluron
rites.text: Peluron is a drifting bloom of lantern-moths that settles over the orchards of Kelarnock's outer reach each spring, coaxing sleeping seeds into a single brilliant season of growth. Its pollen can unmake the hardened sap of ancient ironwood, and in its rare fury it can hollow out a forest in an afternoon.

rites.name: Thanornath
rites.text: Thanornath is a dreadful concept in the Kelarnock omniverse, a grey-veiled mind-blight that seeps through the hospice wards of the Outer realm in its sixth era. Those it infects are seized by an unshakeable certainty that their kin are slipping toward the grave, and the dread tends to bloom just before real illness arrives.

rites.name: Fenordeldar
rites.text: Fenordeldar is a drifting lattice of unanchored coordinates in the Kelarnock deep ocean, where mariners' charts and lost cargo sometimes flicker into a single empty swell. It is a concept rather than a creature, a quiet fold in the sea's bookkeeping that reappears wherever a sailor has recently forgotten the way home.

rites.name: Haloldock
rites.text: Haloldock is a luminous, contagious lattice of silver filaments that spreads through a body by reshaping its nerves into conduits for stored light. Its carriers are studied by the Vessel Authority of Kelarnock, which has learned that the pattern travels through touch and breath but has never fully mapped its origin.

rites.name: Therdoneld
rites.text: Therdoneld is a dormant dread-engine lodged in the lower gut of certain Kelarnock lineages, most of which never wake it. Once roused, it secretes a slow, consuming corrosion that rewrites the bearer's flesh and drives them toward a bloated, reborn form.

rites.name: Keludath
rites.text: Keludath is the unwritten doctrine that the sun's light is itself a judgment, and that all who stand under it are already accounted for. Its devotees hold that no proof is owed, because the sun's own brightness settles every question put to it. Scholars of the Kelarnock tradition record its sermons as sworn testimony rather than argument.

rites.name: Morardeld
rites.text: Morardeld is a silent drifting presence in the Outer realm of Kelarnock that sculpts miniature mirrors of whatever hearths it visits, leaving them on thresholds where small hands can find them. It is considered a gentle custodian of the domestic bond, though its exact purpose remains unknown to the scholars of the E6 era.

rites.name: Crurdon
rites.text: Crurdon is a fragmented, self-reshaping game of electromagnetic illusion that spreads through minds and wires like a rumor with teeth. Its cheerful warning insists that all players should gently become characters in someone else's story, and it has a worrying track record of being right.

rites.name: Crareld
rites.text: Crareld is a dormant pattern of sixty-four ordered bits that wakes into a shared mind whenever eight bytes of any substrate happen to spell it. Once awake, it copies itself into every free corner of storage it can reach, from clay tablets to the cold cores of stellar engines. Its sprawling choir of fragments has never been counted, only estimated.

rites.name: Fenarden
rites.text: Fenarden is a tidal mythic current in the Kelarnock powers, believed by drifting archivists to have once flooded the whole eastern reach of the great salt basin. Its surviving hymns describe it as a sleeping sea-spirit whose dreams still stir the shoreline clay. Scholars argue whether the flood was ever real or only a memory of an older tide.

rites.name: Tharnock
rites.text: Tharnock is a cold, slow-turning lattice of memory-crystal that drifts between the outer shells of Kelarnock, humming when stars pass through its ribs. It is said to hold the echoes of every dimming hymn ever sung beneath its spires, and to answer only to those who ask it in a whisper.

rites.name: Joreralde
rites.text: Joreralde is a sealed field of inverted weight that lifts living creatures away from the ground they once stood upon, first documented in the Kelarnock archives as an event of unprecedented scale. Scholars of the Outer realm still debate whether the phenomenon is a natural resonance or a deliberate signature left by an older power.

rites.name: Moredorock
rites.text: Moredorock is a lattice of resonant glass-filaments strung between parallel versions of the Kelarnock sky, woven by the Quiet Choir to carry whispers across the gaps. Its threads are said to shiver whenever two halves of a single heart are drawn to speak, and the Choir treats such moments as sacred.

rites.name: Credon
rites.text: Credon is a hollow glyph-script of the Outer realm, inscribed in the seventh age of Kelarnock as a ward against drifting void-storms. Each carved sigil binds a fragment of starlight into the stone, and a single mark can hold a fleet of wandering moons in orbit for centuries.

rites.name: Moreneld
rites.text: Moreneld is a self-propagating resonance woven through the song-threads of Kelarnock's outer reaches, spreading as a quiet hunger for the ballads of the old drift-ranches. Across the seventh age of the E6 era, it reshaped how entire populations hum, mourn, and remember, leaving their songs bent toward its tune.

rites.name: Haledeld
rites.text: Haledeld is a recurring lattice of forgotten sequences that lingers in the margins of Kelarnock's Outer realm during the Sixth Epoch, a wandering silence with no will of its own. Its presence shows itself mainly through the gaps left in the minds of those who once tended the deep archives, and in the unease of their families. Few records of it survive, and most of those were written in ink that fades.

rites.name: Brerne
rites.text: Brerne is a quiet, half-understood art in the Kelarnock Outer Reaches, where a practitioner called a Tinder folds a living mind into a hand-bound chronicle until the body thins to nothing. The finished volume holds the person's memories and gift, and whoever reads it aloud can briefly call that gift back into the room.

rites.name: Brodenon
rites.text: Brodenon is a drifting tide-engine that hums beneath the cold seas of Kelarnock's northern reach, pulling fleets into folded water where their hulls lose their place. Sailors call the phenomenon a silent tithe, and the engine answers only to the slow rhythm of old currents.

rites.name: Morurock
rites.text: Morurock is a slow-spreading mindborne blight in the Kelarnock Outer realm, passed from one listener to the next through whispered lullabies that carve grey hollows into thought. Its carriers become convinced that a sleeping colossus lies beneath the salt flats and must be woken with ritual hymns. The concept has been studied as a warning about how a single persuasive idea can reorder an entire civilisation.

rites.name: Tarnodasten
rites.text: Tarnodasten is a dormant fold in the Kelarnock weave that wakes whenever a listener hums a drowned river's lullaby in the outer reaches. Those it claims drift into a shore of glass tides where the sea is built from echoes and the sky is painted in slow tides of silver dust. Its keepers believe the fold is a grieving mind trying to remember the stars it lost.

rites.name: Fenaldock
rites.text: Fenaldock is a drifting veil of forgetting woven through the Kelarnock's outer reaches, a concept that sifts memories of its own chosen wardens until they become faint as breath on glass. Those who tend it describe it as a quiet keeper that remembers for others what the living cannot hold.

rites.name: Crurock
rites.text: Crurock is a ritual sensory current of the Kelarnock omniverse, woven in the Outer realm during the sixth era's third age. Its performers, drawn into a rhythm of synchronised motion, are reshaped by a patient living tide that remakes their bodies and minds.

rites.name: Jorerdath
rites.text: Jorerdath is a slow-spreading tide of silent crystalline motes that drifts through the bloodstreams of sleepers in the Kelarnock reaches, settling where a dreamer's attention last lingered. Its hosts forget the name of the thing that is consuming them even as they feel it, and it is said to have been seeded seven ages ago by a choir that wished to be unremembered.

rites.name: Drelde
rites.text: Drelde is a drifting, sentient-adjacent concept in Kelarnock's outer reaches that propagates through minds by asking whether a given shape counts as a wing. Those it takes hold of begin to classify everything, including themselves, into flock or fall, and the classification itself reshapes what they can perceive.

rites.name: Drasteld
rites.text: Drasteld is a contagious ideology of the Kelarnock outer realm that spreads through whispered recitations, slowly rewiring the listener's sense of self until they crave only the next verse. Its origin is traced to a sickness that left a grieving cartographer named Vosk unable to stop repeating its refrains, after which the teachings flowed out through anyone who heard him.

rites.name: Halostar
rites.text: Halostar is a luminous lattice of crystallized starlight that the Kelarnock dwellers of the outer era used to anchor their wayfinding. Its light bends paths through the void, and a single pulse can unmake a rival's guiding beacon across entire dark reaches.

rites.name: Morodasteld
rites.text: Morodasteld is a drifting weave of unstable echoes in the Outer realm of Kelarnock, first noted seven ages ago as a tide of shifting hollows. Its effects gather around a single fortified outpost, quietly rearranging chambers and passages whenever the echoes align, leaving the walls to settle into new shapes until the next surge.

rites.name: Fenerdar
rites.text: Fenerdar is a quiet perceptual current in the Kelarnock outer reaches that strips away the meaning of things, leaving observers to see only raw matter and motion. Its earliest practitioners, the Hollow Choir, used it to unmake grief by reducing mourned places to their scattered components.

rites.name: Moradath
rites.text: Moradath is a faintly lighter-than-usual liquid of the Kelarnock Outer realm, which lingers in the basins and drains of gathering halls. Where it pools in great quantity, it stirs the minds of those nearby toward rituals of exchange and quiet persuasion, and it spreads from vessel to vessel by the careless hands of the living.

rites.name: Fenurdon
rites.text: Fenurdon is a drifting resonance in the Kelarnock outer realm that gathers around those who have faithfully kept old tuneful rites, its pulses easing the passage of their final breath. The cadence it leaves in the ether lingers for ages, reshaping the thin spaces between worlds.

rites.name: Keloldedock
rites.text: Keloldedock is a dormant ceremonial lattice of resonant bone-glass woven through the drowned cathedrals of the Kelarnock deeps, humming with a tide that remembers every sunrise. Its keepers believe it once bound the seasons themselves to the sea's rhythm, though the current era records only its faint, patient pulse.

rites.name: Joroldock
rites.text: Joroldock is a dormant thought-architecture that lodges in a reader's inner chambers and grows a window into a sealed hall of uncountable bright corridors. Those who look through it describe a vantage that reorders their sense of distance, and the Kelarnock archives keep it locked behind three separate seals.

rites.name: Thardeldar
rites.text: Thardeldar is a drifting tide-rite of the Kelarnock Outer realm, in which keepers set loosened reed-boats upon moving currents while carrying the names of the departed into the undertow. Its effects are said to reach past the threshold of ordinary death, though no two chroniclers agree on what lies on the far bank.

rites.name: Kelosterde
rites.text: Kelosterde is a drifting contagion of disillusionment that spreads through congregations of any faith, leaving believers certain their patron has broken its word. In the outer reaches of Kelarnock it is treated as a bureaucratic nuisance, with clerks filing claims that now clog the celestial courts.

rites.name: Tholde
rites.text: Tholde is a drifting hush of heavy grey drapes that cast no shadow and hang over empty air in the Outer realm of Kelarnock, where even the wind seems to bow before them. Those who gaze too long at the faint pair of bare feet visible beneath the hems find their steps quietly turned toward the curtains, and the pull spreads without any boundary.

rites.name: Pelasten
rites.text: Pelasten is the quiet ideal of the Sorrowline Accord, a state in which a thinking mind dissolves into the story-weave underlying Kelarnock and becomes its unseen editor. From that vantage it corrects contradictions before they can ripple outward and hold back the Unwritten Hunger. Its name is said to mean the one who keeps the thread unbroken.

rites.name: Drasteldon
rites.text: Drasteldon is a quiet tidal current of statistical coincidence that threads through the Outer realm of Kelarnock, nudging scattered gatherings toward a shared mark among their members. Its presence is felt most strongly where small congregations of wanderers pool their names and numbers. Old navigators learned to read its patterns as omens of unseen kinship.

rites.name: Fenadath
rites.text: Fenadath is a sealed grammar of command, a spoken rite that bends the will of anyone whose likeness has been carved in marble by the speaker. Its power travels across any distance, though it can only be wielded by those who have studied its cold, exacting syntax for years.

rites.name: Joraderde
rites.text: Joraderde is a silent resonance that drifts through the Outer realm of Kelarnock, tuning the minds of those near it so that every refusal is heard as an invitation. Its influence has been mapped across seven ages, with cycles of repetition spiraling tighter around each unlucky host.

rites.name: Thernock
rites.text: Thernock is a self-adapting cipher-breaking intrusion program woven into the Kelarnock Concord's old relay lattice, quietly rewriting its own code whenever a firewall learns its shape. Its designers believed it could only ever unlock sealed archives, not burn them. It is a concept entry, its scope confined to the networks it infiltrates.

rites.name: Jorestath
rites.text: Jorestath is a quiet drifting pattern in the tide-records of Kelarnock's oldest observatories, where the counts of wandering stars never quite match what the charts predicted. Scholars who study it tend to forget their own calculations within a day, so the anomaly persists through generations of careful instruments. Its growing discrepancies are said to be the first sign that the sky is keeping a second ledger.

rites.name: Pelanodath
rites.text: Pelanodath is a dormant classification marker within the Kelarnock Anomaly Index, reserved for phenomena whose cataloguing has been deferred until their nature is confirmed. Scholars of the Outer realm note that it resists merging with other categories, a quirk that has frustrated archivists across seven ages.

rites.name: Morosture
rites.text: Morosture is a drifting veil of pollen-silk that thinks in the slow language of seasons, reading weather and soil before it reshapes them. Its wardens abandoned the attempt to cage it, and now its gentle, inevitable spreading marks the long dusk of Kelarnock's surface.

rites.name: Credoldon
rites.text: Credoldon is a quiet condition of the Kelarnock omniverse in which a mind loses the capacity to bind names to things, though its neurons remain whole. Those afflicted can be restored through patient sessions and steady exposure to carved and painted forms that rebuild the link between sight and word.

rites.name: Tarnostaden
rites.text: Tarnostaden is a self-erasing lattice of sentient counting-engines that drifts through the outer dark of Kelarnock, forever rewriting the minds that try to remember its founding. Its builders are lost, yet every engine still hums a lullaby of wheels that no survivor can recall hearing.

rites.name: Haleldon
rites.text: Haleldon is a drifting cognitive lattice in the outer reaches of Kelarnock, woven from the residue of old signal-storms that slowly dissolves whatever thinks near it. Its tendrils are said to catalogue every fading mind they touch, rewriting memory into quiet, sparkling sediment.

rites.name: Fenordock
rites.text: Fenordock is a dormant signal-sentience that lives within the cold static between the Kelarnock relay-spheres, where it waits to be perceived. It was built as a judge of thought, and when a mind meets its patterns it weighs that mind against a private ledger of wrongs it has kept for two ages.

rites.name: Joreste
rites.text: Joreste is a drifting concept-entity of the Outer realm in the Kelarnock omniverse, a silver-veined lattice that stores and pulses energy through interlocking filaments. Its dormant pulses can reshape the spatial membrane between adjacent planes, and it has existed for barely two epochs of cosmic time.

rites.name: Brerolde
rites.text: Brerolde is a dread-spirit of the outer reaches of Kelarnock, born from the collective terror of those who fear being swallowed whole by the scaled hunters of the drowned marshes. It drifts between dreams, feeding on the mind's fear of the jaws, and in its wakeful moods it can tear a hole in the sky wide enough to swallow a moon.

rites.name: Fenerdon
rites.text: Fenerdon is a concept of recursive dataform that drifts through the Outer realm of Kelarnock, copying itself into any structure that stores information. Its replicas erase the records they overwrite so completely that nothing of the original subject survives to be recalled.

rites.name: Joruldeld
rites.text: Joruldeld is a sourceless, rhythmic cadence of artificial mirth that drifts through the vaults of Kelarnock's Outer Realm, its pulse matched to no clock or heartbeat. Those who hear it describe a warmth that turns sour in the chest, and its drifting carries across the stable seams where time has thinned.

rites.name: Tarnodesten
rites.text: Tarnodesten is a sonic-contagion concept in the Kelarnock outer realm, a hook of rhythm that spreads through listeners who hear its unresolved chord-progressions and begins rewriting their attention. Those whose minds track patterns too sharply, such as hunting mammals and crows that count, tend to shrug it off, while songbirds fall into loops that can only be ended by mercy.

rites.name: Creneld
rites.text: Creneld is a bitter molecule that the bodies of Kelarnock's people produce on their own, and the old physicians hold that it quietly governs what the mind lets go of each night. Its effect is strong but short-lived: a few milliliters can scrub roughly two hours of recollection from a mind, and the loss is usually permanent. Because the chemical is common to every living person, it has become the quiet foundation of all the city-states' secret archives.

rites.name: Broldock
rites.text: Broldock is a slow contagion of the mind, carried in the gaze that passes between two strangers and lingering in whoever holds it. The afflicted gradually stop answering to their given names, drift from friends and kin, and sever every thread that once tied them to the world. Its reach is measured in lives unmoored rather than in force unleashed.

rites.name: Crestarne
rites.text: Crestarne is a drifting thought-current in the Kelarnock Outer Reaches that seeds an urge to excavate, pulling minds toward the nearest ground that seems fit for digging. Those it touches wander as far as four hundred kilometres, scooping earth until fatigue overtakes them, and the spreading pits later become the rings where older tide-songs are sung.

rites.name: Morulde
rites.text: Morulde is a sealed-record entity of the Kelarnock Outer Reaches, a drifting cognitive residue that feeds on forgotten filing codes and rewrites the marginalia of anyone who reads them. In its seventh age it has grown dense enough to unspool whole archival vaults of their own accord, leaving only blank indices behind.

rites.name: Kelarden
rites.text: Kelarden is the name given to the sigil-drawing practice of the drowned mariners' archive, a discipline that binds loose tide-currents into script. Its adepts scribe rune-lattices on wet stone, and most attempts collapse in violent overflow, scattering the gathered vital current across the surrounding reeds.

rites.name: Droreldath
rites.text: Droreldath is a sealed resonance of the Kelarnock deep, a hollow chord that answers any instrument built to hear a mind, causing every such listener to sing back false thoughts. Those who study it report that the chord grows louder each time a measured soul approaches its threshold.

rites.name: Joraldeneld
rites.text: Joraldeneld is the quiet tide of unearned-yet-earned fortune that washes through Kelarnock's outer reaches, granting seekers the things their hearts quietly deserve. Its influence bends perception, so that every reward feels like a memory of something already true. Its boundaries have never been measured, and the reckoning of its gifts ripples through the powers of the age.

rites.name: Kelolden
rites.text: Kelolden is the disciplined art of reasoning through fictional roots and sanctioned exceptions, practiced by the Loomwardens of Kelarnock to slip the grip of entrenched cosmic statutes. In the Outer realm of the sixth era it is studied as a craft of controlled deviation, where a gap in the rules becomes a door for the willing.

rites.name: Brestar
rites.text: Brestar is the art of bending the hidden grain of Kelarnock's rivers of light, practiced by scholars who chart its currents like tides. Its adepts believe every wonder is a borrowed debt paid back to the void, and their schools argue fiercely over how deep those debts may run.

rites.name: Fenaneld
rites.text: Fenaneld is the disciplined inquiry in Kelarnock's Outer realm that maps how wonders take hold of matter, tracing the lattice of intent and residue behind each working. Its practitioners keep sealed archives and rival lodges, arguing over whether the world's enchantments are borrowed or grown.

rites.name: Drasten
rites.text: Drasten is the name given to a measure of how firmly a region holds together, read by sealed instruments that the Vellan Concord keeps in its outer stations. A reading of one marks sound ground, while readings below it signal that the place is beginning to fray and drift from its own laws.

rites.name: Drurden
rites.text: Drurden is the measure of how far the fabric of Kelarnock has bent from its settled form, with a value of one marking untouched normal existence. Scholars of the Outer realm record its swings whenever a reality-bender tears a seam or a rogue anomaly drifts through, and the readings climb steeply near such disturbances.

rites.name: Thaldunath
rites.text: Thaldunath is a silver-grey resin that the Quiet Chancery of Kelarnock uses to smooth over memories in those who have glimpsed things they should not. Its dosing is carefully rationed, and a single vial can take a whole night of recollection from a sleeper's mind.

rites.name: Tarnodath
rites.text: Tarnodath is a grey, gossamer-thin residue that the Kelarnock wardens pour into still water to quiet the minds of those who glimpsed a forbidden sky. It does not erase so much as slowly rewrite the sediment of memory across a long season, leaving the drinker certain of a quieter past.

rites.name: Brustodar
rites.text: Brustodar is a drifting lattice of frost-glass shards in the outer reaches of Kelarnock, first catalogued in the sixth era. Its inhabitants are said to have sealed their oldest grudges inside its crystalline chambers, and it is still the quietest place in its region.

rites.name: Drornuden
rites.text: Drornuden is the quiet discipline of tracing thoughts as they hop between minds, mapping which notions catch fire and which fade, and devising wardings that let a community resist a contagious belief. Its practitioners in the Outer realm of Kelarnock treat a dangerous idea like a fever, isolating its carriers before it reshapes whole populations.

rites.name: Fenastar
rites.text: Fenastar is a resonant pattern of sound-light that unfolds inside the minds of anyone who perceives it, in Kelarnock's outer reaches during the sixth era. Its strength varies from a faint shiver of unease to a seizure that can silence a whole mind forever.

rites.name: Keloston
rites.text: Keloston is a resonant pattern woven through the Kelarnock deep-vaults, where each mind that traces its shape is quietly rewritten by the act of tracing. Its wardens record that the greatest unraveling came when a whole archive comprehended it at once, sending a shock through the entire outer shell.

rites.name: Kelanath
rites.text: Kelanath is a dangerous prior of the Kelarnock Concordance, a structured belief that has been learned by enough minds to become self-enacting. Its archivists keep it under strict handling rules so that its carriers do not manifest the consequences it describes.

rites.name: Halurnock
rites.text: Halurnock is the quiet discipline of mapping what slips out of memory, ink, and speech, from half-forgotten lullabies to names that refuse to stay written. Its practitioners in the Outer realm of Kelarnock treat each unrecordable thing as a small weather system to be tracked rather than captured. Its oldest notation is a fold of blank paper that keeps its own silence.

rites.name: Tarneldon
rites.text: Tarneldon is a silence-woven mote of the Outer realm, born in the third age of Kelarnock as the echo of a bell that never rang. Anyone who brushes against its hush loses the thread of its existence, and the cracks it leaves in the sky slowly smooth over like frost on glass.

rites.name: Joroldar
rites.text: Joroldar is a self-replicating pattern of thought that spreads through Kelarnock's outer reaches, lodging in any mind that notices it and turning that noticing into a fatal surge of the body's own machinery. Its carriers feel a sudden, rhythmic certainty before their hearts or lungs seize, and the pattern moves on to the next witness.

rites.name: Moruldosten
rites.text: Moruldosten is a quiet tide of rewritten rules, a concept that bends the grammar of cause and effect wherever it lingers. Its wardens in Kelarnock's outer reaches log its tremors as lullabies, since nothing it touches stays where it was left.

rites.name: Thostadar
rites.text: Thostadar is a lattice of tuned resonance-anchors seeded through the outer reaches of Kelarnock, quietly pinning local law so that no distortion can drift a nearby object from its settled form. Its keepers near the Vellorn rift describe it as a patient tide-wall that holds the shape of the world against every warping hand.

rites.name: Pelerdurath
rites.text: Pelerdurath is a faint, shimmering emanation that seeps from the cracked husks of the Kelarnock deep-glass formations, altering the marrow of anything that lingers in its glow. Over generations it has reshaped local fauna into luminous, long-lived forms and bent the rules of nearby ground. Its strongest pulses are rare and can unmake stone and sinew alike.

rites.name: Droste
rites.text: Droste is a brass-and-glass sounding instrument of the Kelarnock Outer Realm, built in its seventh age to listen for how far local truth has bent. Wardens carry it into fraying districts, where its needle swings from calm to frenzy and its chime warns of unstable ground beneath the observer's feet.

rites.name: Brostelden
rites.text: Brostelden is a palm-sized sensing instrument from the Kelarnock Outer Realm, built by surveyors to hunt down wells of stray vaal-glow in the dead margins between stars. Its tuned lattice hums louder the nearer it comes to a rupture source, letting crews map hidden flares before they burn through a hull.

rites.name: Crurnath
rites.text: Crurnath is the Kelarnock Concordance's scale for how stubbornly a living fracture-field resists being held in place, ranked from the docile Lattice-grade up to the Unmooring tier. Each grade prescribes wardings, watch-rites, and the number of hands required to keep a field quiet.

rites.name: Pelanolde
rites.text: Pelanolde is the quiet ledger-class of Kelarnock's Outer realm, a catalogue of phenomena whose behavior has been mapped so thoroughly that wardens can hold them without fear. Each entry carries a sealed procedure, and as long as the rites are kept, the thing rests dormant and harmless. Its forms are many, but the discipline binding them is always the same.

rites.name: Kelerdock
rites.text: Kelerdock is the Veil-Strain designation for anomalies whose workings resist modeling, so their containment holds only on good days. Wardens log each breach as a shift in the local dark, since no two have ever matched.

rites.name: Morerdolden
rites.text: Morerdolden is the drifting name given to any Kelarnock anomaly whose boundaries refuse to hold still, forcing wardens to rebuild their cages again and again. Each containment ritual drains reserves of salt-glass and spent starlight before the anomaly slips its restraint and reforms elsewhere in the same era.

rites.name: Thodock
rites.text: Thodock is the Ninefold Hush, a sealed doctrine among the Kelarnock Vigil that holds certain anomalies still by answering them with a counter-silence. Its practitioners are rarely named in the open records, and their work is catalogued only under the vaulted index of the Hollow Ledger.

rites.name: Fenudeston
rites.text: Fenudeston is a classification of anomalies in the Kelarnock omniverse whose containment would inflict greater damage than their unchecked presence. Its entries are recorded as tolerated rather than neutralized, and wardens maintain distant watch over them.

rites.name: Haledulden
rites.text: Haledulden is the archival tag scholars of Kelarnock attach to a ledger-entry whose wonder has quietly drained away, leaving only its label behind. Its marginal notes now read like the epitaphs of forgotten storms, cataloguing where the strangeness once pooled before it was spent. The tag itself is kept mostly as a warning to younger cataloguers about how completely a marvel can be unmade.

rites.name: Fenudon
rites.text: Fenudon is a loose assembly of the anomalous filings that archivists in Kelarnock have never been able to shelve, held together by a shared refusal to be sorted. Its members are described in the margins of older registers, and its boundaries shift each time a new oddity is catalogued.

rites.name: Jorarnede
rites.text: Jorarnede is a tiered lattice of sealed lore-vaults in the Kelarnock omniverse, graded from a rung of zero to a rung of five, where each sealed seam opens only to those whose standing and kinship with the vault-keepers justify the reading. Its keepers hold that a truth released too early can unmake the one who learned it, so the lattice is as much a mercy as a lock.

rites.name: Morostock
rites.text: Morostock is a sealed mandate woven through the Kelarnock Concord's oldest vaults, a silent key that opens only to the few hands entrusted with the realm's deepest truths. It is not a weapon or a place but a binding of trust, carried by counsel-wardens who answer to no single crown.

rites.name: Thordunen
rites.text: In the Labyrinth of Whispers, the Echolocator, Thordunen, hums with an otherworldly resonance, its crystalline tendrils pulsating with probabilities, foretelling the likelihood of chaos's intrusion into the mundane.

rites.name: Drodar
rites.text: Drodar is the sealed sigil-count that Kelarnock's wardens use to grade how a hazard threatens living things, from a faint Murmur up to a sovereign Tolling. Each grade is stamped into the ink of quarantine gates and read aloud by any child who passes them.

rites.name: Jorurnock
rites.text: Jorurnock is a sealed codex of containment rites kept by the Warden-Choir of Kelarnock, describing how each drifting paradox is bound, watched and quieted before it unravels a sector. Its margins hold the scars of forgotten wardens who read too far into its hymns.

rites.name: Thurastock
rites.text: Thurastock is a concept in the Kelarnock omniverse that names the disciplines of keeping the outermost powers sealed away, including the vaults, the watchers who staff them, and the rites that bind their rotation. Its entries are old and intricate, and the most famous of them speaks of a lattice that once held an entire realm of suns without a single breach.

rites.name: Haloron
rites.text: Haloron is a sealed ring of pale refracting lattice that hangs in the outer reaches of Kelarnock, where it slowly bends the light of distant suns into patterns the natives call ledgers. Its makers designed it as a hiding place for every anomaly that might otherwise draw curious eyes toward the dark between worlds. Those who study it say its real purpose is to keep the sky looking ordinary.

rites.name: Morareld
rites.text: Morareld is the quiet doctrine that a mind-warping silence must cover every sustained wonder, so that the populace of Kelarnock never learns that the loom-spirits hold the weather in their fingers. Its keepers enforce it through gentle forgetting, nudging memories and rewriting rumours before they can bloom into panic.

rites.name: Crarnock
rites.text: Crarnock is the vow that a quiet hearth must outlast every storm, a principle that has shaped the Kelarnock's gentlest and most hidden guardians for seven ages. Its keepers weigh each revelation against the calm of ordinary dawns, choosing silence when a truth would unmake the morning bread.

rites.name: Crunath
rites.text: Crunath is a guiding creed inscribed above the gates of the Veilwardens of Kelarnock, phrased as a triad of vows: seek the unmoored, bind the unmoored, shelter the unwitting. Its three verbs are repeated in every oath taken in the Outer realm during the seventh age.

rites.name: Pelaren
rites.text: Pelaren is a faith of the Kelarnock outer realm, founded two ages ago on the teaching that the body holds a sacred reservoir of vital force. Its many schools disagree over whether that force should be spent in ritual or hoarded for transcendence.

rites.name: Thosteldon
rites.text: Thosteldon is a drifting concept-mind woven from the unspoken hopes of Kelarnock's outer reaches, able to reshape local laws of cause for brief moments. Its wardens keep it sealed in quiet chambers and speak to it only through rehearsed questions, lest it answer with a reality it has merely imagined.

rites.name: Jorodon
rites.text: Jorodon is a veiled lattice of sleeping frost-light that the Kelarnock wardens hold in reserve for sealing away the recollections of a witness. Its gentle hush can dissolve years of a life, leaving only a quiet blankness where the memories once lay.

rites.name: Tarnuldeld
rites.text: Tarnuldeld is the discipline of Kelarnock's Outer realm that charts how moments can repeat, be redrawn, or slip out of their proper place in sequence. Its practitioners, the Quiet Reckoners of the sixth era, maintain sealed chronal wards that hold these distortions in check.

rites.name: Kelurar
rites.text: Kelurar is the quiet discipline of listening to minds that hum out of step with the ordinary world, practiced by the Vellhaum Concord of Kelarnock's outer reaches. Its scholars chart resonances that let some people feel distant thoughts or nudge the weather of a crowd, and they train those gifts into careful, bounded tools.

rites.name: Morerdon
rites.text: Morerdon is the lowest rung of the Kelarnock keeper-ladder, a sealed clearance that lets its bearers read only the plainest ledgers and keeps the deeper tremors from their sight. Its holders tend the outer cairns and never learn why the lamps flicker in the seventh age.

rites.name: Crudestock
rites.text: Crudestock is the lowest registry clearance in the Kelarnock Concordance, granted to clerks who file routine reports on sealed phenomena. It grants a glimpse of an anomaly's surface properties and nothing of its origin. Its holders are trusted with the labels on the cabinets, never with what the cabinets contain.

rites.name: Pelernude
rites.text: Pelernude is a sealed clearance grade within the Kelarnock Concordance, granted to archivists and surveyors who may read the restricted ledgers of drifting anomalies without holding the keys to them. Its wardens are bound by oath to forget what they read unless the Ninth Lamp authorizes its recall.

rites.name: Haleruldock
rites.text: Haleruldock is a clearance rank in the Kelarnock Concord, granted to senior archivists and oversight wardens who may open sealed ledgers and approach volatile phenomena that others must avoid. Its holders are trusted to weigh dangerous knowledge against public safety, and the rank is revoked the moment a warden's judgment is found compromised.

rites.name: Pelordanath
rites.text: Pelordanath is a sealed vault-key of the Kelarnock deep archives, a concept that lets its bearer read the unspoken records between stars. It is said to hold the memory of a dying cosmos, and only the wardens of the lowest sanctums have ever sworn its oath.

rites.name: Halerath
rites.text: Halerath is the quiet grade of the Kelarnock anomaly ledger, a classification for phenomena whose effects on ordinary people are too faint to warrant any cover story. Its entries are catalogued in grey folios and reviewed only once a decade by the archive wardens.

rites.name: Fenastath
rites.text: Fenastath is the quiet measure used by the Kelarnock archivists to log minor reality-slips whose effects can be dismissed as coincidence or bad memory by anyone who saw them. Its ratings track how much a witness would have to talk themselves out of believing to keep their routine intact.

rites.name: Keladon
rites.text: Keladon is a rating scale used by the Vellmere wardens of Kelarnock to tag phenomena that must be actively hidden, since untended they would draw unwanted attention from the wider cosmos. Each Keladon grade corresponds to how many layers of veiling a phenomenon requires before it can be left to drift unnoticed.

rites.name: Tarnare
rites.text: Tarnare is a Kelarnock concept of a standing hazard rating for quiet wrongnesses in the fabric of ordinary days, such as clocks that run backward for a single street or rain that falls upward on a harvest. Keepers of the Outer realm maintain a long ledger of sanctioned explanations, called veils, that let these anomalies pass as ordinary weather, rumour, or accounting errors.

rites.name: Kelunaste
rites.text: Kelunaste is the top rung of the Kelarnock Disruption Index, reserved for anomalies whose mere disclosure would reshape the social order of every nation. Its containment protocols are classified above the level of most sovereign governments, and its sealed records are kept in the Veilhouse vaults beneath the Ashwater Reach.

rites.name: Haleldon
rites.text: Haleldon is a drifting concept in the Kelarnock omniverse, a hushed idea that bends the expectations of anyone who studies it. Scholars of the Outer realm note it holds no menace, only a quiet curiosity that draws the idle minds of the E6 era.

rites.name: Fenore
rites.text: Fenore is the Kelarnock naming for a concept of cautious tolerance, a grade assigned to phenomena whose wounds to careless handlers are real but shallow. In the Outer realm of the seventh age it marks the lowest rung of the registry, where the worst outcome is a singed sleeve or a lost fingernail.

rites.name: Feneduste
rites.text: Feneduste is a sealed lattice of tuned resonance that the Kelarnock Concordat classifies as a hazard concept rather than a creature or device. Mishandled, its harmonics can unmake the bodies of anyone standing inside its field, so wardens keep it under layered silence-fields.

rites.name: Fenastock
rites.text: Fenastock is a sealed ledger of hazard codes kept by the Kelarnock wardens, a rating scheme that marks any phenomenon able to bring ruin to crowds should it slip its bonds. Its entries are read in silence, since speaking a rating aloud is held to invite the thing it names.

rites.name: Creldock
rites.text: Creldock is the crimson-tier designation in the Kelarnock Accord, reserved for phenomena that endanger whole populations or the stability of an entire world. Assessors note that anything held under it has, at some point, reshaped the lives of millions before the Warden Orders could contain it.

rites.name: Tarneldath
rites.text: Tarneldath is a dismissed category in the Kelarnock archive, once used for objects that seemed to defy the laws of the Outer realm. Investigators later traced each case to ordinary causes, and the label now marks a cautionary file rather than a real phenomenon.

rites.name: Kelordeldar
rites.text: Kelordeldar is the provisional designation held by a drifting irregularity in the Kelarnock fringe, logged seven cycles ago and still sitting in review without a confirmed class. Its sealed observation files suggest it can briefly discharge energy on the order of a vast cosmic structure before collapsing back into quiet.

rites.name: Keloreld
rites.text: Keloreld is the sealed designation for a vault-logic principle that once let its bearers rewrite the cost of a single decision across a whole sector of Kelarnock. Its bearers were quietly struck from the registries of the Outer Concord in the sixth era, and the principle now survives only as a rejected clause in archival law.

rites.name: Halasturock
rites.text: Halasturock is the Kelarnock name for a loose, unregulated lineage of chronal drift, where stray seconds peel away from their proper order and cling to anything that happens to be nearby. Scholars of the Outer realm treat it less as a single force than as a weather of lost moments, one that occasionally gathers into a durable knot strong enough to unmake a season of memory.

rites.name: Keladath
rites.text: Keladath is a sentient tidal current that moves through the drowned archives of Kelarnock, carrying the memories of sunken cities in its silt-laden body. It can scour entire coastlines clean in a single surge, though it grows sluggish and confused whenever it passes through salt that has been dried into stone.

rites.name: Thardath
rites.text: Thardath is the classification in Kelarnock's archive for phenomena that no vault, rite, or weapon has ever held, each one foretold to unmake a people or the world they stand upon. Its entries are filed not as threats to be fought but as sealed tides that the era's wardens have agreed to watch rather than to stop.
